The strategies and outcomes can be summarized as follows:
- If both players cooperate, they each get a moderate reward, say \(R\).
- If one player defects while the other cooperates, the defector gets a very high reward, say \(T\), while the cooperator gets the lowest possible reward, say \(P\).
- If both players defect, they each get a reward, say \(P\).

The dilemma can be described in the following payoff matrix:

\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
\text{Player 2} & \text{Cooperate} & \text{Defect} \\
\hline
\text{Cooperate} & (R, R) & (P, T) \\
\text{Defect} & (T, P) & (P, P) \\
\end{array}
\]

To decide what to choose, consider the following:
- If you know that Player 2 will cooperate, you should defect and get \(T\).
- If you know that Player 2 will defect, you should defect and get \(P\).

In the real scenario where you do not have information about what Player 2 will do, you must choose a strategy that maximizes your payoff given the choices available to you.

- If Player 2 cooperates, you will get \(T\).
